transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I'm here because... well, I've started doing some things lately that are really starting to scare me. I'm a computer systems analyst, and lately I've just been... walking out in the middle of major software deployments. Just leaving. And at night, I've been driving around really late, just aimlessly, with no plan or destination. It's reckless, and it's just... it's not me. I've never handled stress this way before, and I don't know what's going on.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most of the day?
No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I mean, I'm definitely worried about my behavior, but I haven't been feeling depressed or empty during the day.

Before these recent weeks, did you have a pattern of doing impulsive or reckless things — like suddenly leaving situations, taking unnecessary risks, or acting without thinking — or is this behavior completely new for you?

No, this is completely new. I've never really been an impulsive person. I mean, my job is all about planning and being methodical, so... acting without thinking just isn't like me at all. I've never had a pattern of doing things like this before.

When you have the urge to leave work or drive around late at night, do you feel like you're unable to resist or stop yourself — like there's a strong pull you can't control — or does it feel more like you just aren't thinking things through carefully?

It's more like... I just feel this sudden, overwhelming need to get away. I wouldn't say I'm not thinking things through, it's just that the urge to leave is so strong. It's like a pull I really can't control. I just have to go, right then and there, and I can't seem to stop myself from doing it.
Before you get the urge to leave work or drive around, do you notice a buildup of tension or anxiety that feels relieved once you actually do these things?

Um, no, I haven't really noticed a buildup of tension beforehand. It doesn't slowly build up like that... it just sort of hits me all at once. And I wouldn't say I feel relieved after I drive around or leave, either. It's just a sudden thing I feel like I have to do right in that exact moment.

Did these episodes of suddenly needing to leave or drive around start after a specific event or stressor in your life — like a major change at work, a relationship issue, or something traumatic — or did they just begin out of the blue with no particular trigger?

It definitely started after a specific event, not just out of the blue. Um... this has all been going on since that late-night cutover incident at work. That was a little over a year ago... about 13 months now, I think.

Since that incident 13 months ago, have you been having these urges to leave and drive around pretty much all the time, or do they come and go in episodes with periods where you feel more normal in between?

I'm not entirely sure how to categorize it, to be honest. It's not like I have the urge every single minute of every day, so I guess they come and go. But... I don't really know if I'd say I have long stretches where I feel completely normal in between, either. I haven't really tracked a specific pattern. It just sort of happens when it happens.

When you get these urges to leave work or drive around late at night, do you ever feel disconnected from your body, like you're watching yourself from outside, or does the world around you feel unreal or dreamlike?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. Um, I don't feel disconnected from my body or like I'm watching myself from the outside. The world doesn't feel like a dream, either. I'm very much there and aware of everything... it's just that sudden need to get away.

When you get the urge to leave work or drive around, do you experience it as something you don't want to do but feel unable to stop — like an unwanted thought or impulse pushing you — or does the urge itself feel like something you actually want to do in that moment, even though you know it's not a good idea?

I think it's more that I actually want to do it in that moment. It's not like an unwanted thought forcing me, exactly. It's just... I get this overwhelming feeling that I need to leave, that I have to get out of there, and so I do. I want to leave because staying just feels... wrong, or too much. So I guess the urge feels like something I want to do right then, just to get away.
When you think about that late-night cutover incident from 13 months ago, do you find yourself having unwanted memories or flashbacks of it — or do you ever have nightmares about it?

Yeah, I do get unwanted memories. It's... it happens out of nowhere. Especially if I have to go into that conference area, or if someone on a call raises their voice. When that happens, I just get hit with images and sounds from that night. It's so strong that I'll completely lose track of what I was saying or doing. It just takes over.
